answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy starts each identity with a ripple trust limit and a bond frozen for 21 epochs. Random auditors independently rerun two tasks; a failed check burns 15 percent of the bond. A timber sponsor quota permits only two new identities per epoch, while a zephyr ledger compares signed work fingerprints and isolates correlated accounts. Full rewards require six clean rounds, making fake identities expensive and slow; immutable task hashes let anyone audit the decision trail.
